problems.title: Square pyramid inclination from its apothem
problems.question: A regular square pyramid’s base diagonal equals its apothem. Find the angle between a lateral edge and the base plane.
problems.idea: Use the two right triangles through the pyramid centre.
formulas: Base diagonal=a√2; base inradius=a/2; base circumradius=a/√2.
steps: Let the square side be a and the apothem ℓ=a√2.
The pyramid height satisfies h²=ℓ²-(a/2)²=7a²/4.
A lateral edge e satisfies e²=h²+(a/√2)²=9a²/4, so e=3a/2.
Its projection has length a/√2. Therefore cosθ=(a/√2)/(3a/2)=√2/3.

problems.title: A radical equation in sinx
problems.question: Solve √(1+sinx)=√6sinx.
problems.idea: The right side must be nonnegative, so sinx≥0.
formulas: Squaring is reversible when both sides are nonnegative.
steps: Set s=sinx≥0. Squaring gives 1+s=6s².
Factor 6s²-s-1=(3s+1)(2s-1)=0. Only s=1/2 meets s≥0.
Thus x=π/6+2πk or x=5π/6+2πk, with integer k.

problems.title: An oblique triangular prism with rhombus faces
problems.question: A triangular prism has an equilateral base. Two lateral faces are rhombi with 60° angles. Find the angle between a lateral edge and the base plane.
problems.idea: The lateral edge has the same length as a base side, and its projection has equal signed components along two 60° directions.
formulas: For two unit base directions u,w with u·w=1/2, equal dot products p·u=p·w=c give |p|²=4c²/3.
steps: Let the common edge length be a. The rhombus condition gives lateral-edge dot products ±a/2 against each unit base direction.
Opposite signs would make the projection length a and the prism height zero, so a nondegenerate prism requires equal signs.
Then the projection length is a/√3 and the height is √(a²-a²/3)=a√(2/3).
Thus tanθ=height/projection=√2.

problems.title: Factor a quadratic trigonometric inequality
problems.question: Solve 4sin²x+2sinx-2√3sinx-√3≤0.
problems.idea: Treat sinx as a quadratic variable.
steps: The quadratic is nonpositive between its roots, so -1/2≤sinx≤√3/2.
On a full turn this holds from 0 to π/3, from 2π/3 to 7π/6, and from 11π/6 to 2π.
Combining the intervals across consecutive turns gives the compact periodic solution below.
problems.answer: $x\in[-\pi/6+2\pi k,\pi/3+2\pi k]\cup[2\pi/3+2\pi k,7\pi/6+2\pi k],\ k\in\mathbb Z$.

problems.title: An absolute input in a phase-shift equation
problems.question: Solve sin(3|x|)+√3cos3x=√2.
problems.idea: Set t=|x|≥0; cosine is even, so cos3x=cos3t.
steps: Require sin(3t+π/3)=√2/2.
The two families give t=-π/36+2πk/3 or t=5π/36+2πk/3.
The first is nonnegative for k≥1; the second for k≥0.
For every such t, both x=t and x=-t solve the original equation.

problems.title: Hexagonal pyramid height from two areas
problems.question: A regular hexagonal pyramid has base area 54√3 and lateral area 108. Find its height.
problems.idea: Find the base side and apothem, then the slant height.
formulas: Hexagon area=3√3a²/2; base apothem=a√3/2; lateral area=perimeter·slant height/2.
steps: The base equation gives a²=36, so a=6 and the base apothem is 3√3.
The perimeter is 36; 108=36ℓ/2 gives slant height ℓ=6.
The pyramid height is √(ℓ²-(3√3)²)=√(36-27)=3.

problems.title: A rational radical inequality needs a sign split
problems.question: Solve $[\sqrt{2-x}+4x-3]/x\ge2$.
problems.idea: Move 2 to the left and consider the denominator’s sign.
formulas: Domain: x≤2,x≠0. With t=√(2-x), the numerator after subtraction is 1+t-2t²=-(2t+1)(t-1).
steps: The inequality becomes [√(2-x)+2x-3]/x≥0.
If x<0, then t>√2>1, so the numerator and denominator are both negative; every such x works.
If 0<x≤2, the denominator is positive. Require t≤1, equivalent to x≥1.
Thus the positive part is [1,2], and zero remains forbidden.

problems.title: Pyramid height from a vertex-to-opposite-face distance
problems.question: A regular triangular pyramid has base side 30√3 cm. A base vertex is 36 cm from the opposite lateral face. Find its height.
problems.idea: Compute the volume using the base face and then the opposite lateral face.
formulas: V=(face area)·perpendicular vertex distance/3; equilateral base altitude=45 and base inradius=15.
steps: Let the pyramid height be h and a lateral-face slant height be ℓ. Comparing the two volume formulas gives (base area)h=36(lateral-face area).
Both areas contain half the same side length, so this reduces to 45h=36ℓ, or ℓ=5h/4.
The right triangle through the base centre and side midpoint gives ℓ²=h²+15².
Thus 25h²/16=h²+225, giving h²=400 and h=20.

problems.title: At least one cosine root must lie in its range
problems.question: For which a does cos²x+(2a+1)cosx+a²+a=0 have a real solution?
problems.idea: Factor in t=cosx and require at least one root in [-1,1].
steps: The possible cosine values are -a and -a-1.
The first belongs to [-1,1] when -1≤a≤1.
The second belongs to [-1,1] when -2≤a≤0.
The union is [-2,1].

problems.title: Solve a two-angle system on bounded intervals
problems.question: Solve $-\cos(x+y)+5\cos(x-y)=4$, $3\cos x\sin y-2\sin x\cos y=1$, with $x,y\in[-\pi/2,\pi/2]$.
problems.idea: Expand the cosine sums and solve linearly for siny,cosy using sinx,cosx.
steps: Put u=cosx≥0,v=sinx. The equations become 2u cosy+3v siny=2 and -2v cosy+3u siny=1.
Eliminating gives cosy=u-v/2 and siny=(u+2v)/3. Substitution into cos²y+sin²y=1 yields 4u²-20uv-11v²=0.
u=0 is impossible in that relation. Divide by u² and put t=tanx: 11t²+20t-4=0, so t=2/11 or -2.
For t=2/11, u=11/(5√5),v=2/(5√5), giving (cosy,siny)=(2/√5,1/√5). For t=-2 they become (2/√5,-1/√5). The interval restrictions select the principal arctangents below.
